data.narrative:
ADASI is a sovereign-funded Defense & Security company acquired by EDGE Group. The valuation exercise drew from a Defense & Security comp universe of 10 private and 2 public peers, including Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems among private entities, and DRSHF and IDEAFORGE.NS as public comparables.

The peer-median method was not applicable to this valuation. The Defense & Security sector contains 22 same-sector peers overall, but filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier companies yielded fewer than the three datapoints required for reliable triangulation. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable distortion given the sector's specialized economics, capital intensity, and regulatory environment. No alternative methods—EV/Revenue multiples, precedent transactions, or DCF—produced quantified outputs from the available dataset.

The absence of sufficient narrow peer comparables and the lack of alternative quantitative results leave this valuation unsupported by traditional VC methodology. The sovereign-funded structure and acquisition status further limit applicability of conventional venture metrics. Any valuation range would require external data or transaction precedent not provided in this dataset. The key uncertainty is the absence of transaction multiples or financial metrics sufficient to anchor a defensible range.
